test_title: SSC CHSL (2022) Tier-II Official Paper (Held On: 26 Jun, 2023 Shift 1).
subject: general
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.**

The lawyer told the father of the accused, “There is a rumour that he has some connection in that crime.”

options.text: The lawyer told the father of the accused that there has been a rumour that he had some connection in that crime.
The lawyer told the father of the accused that there was a rumour that he was having some connection in that crime.
The lawyer told the father of the accused that there was a rumour that he had some connection in that crime.
The lawyer told the father of the accused that there was a rumour that he has had some connection in that crime.

solution:
The correct answer is: "**The lawyer told the father of the accused that there was a rumour that he had some connection in that crime.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In indirect speech, the tense of the reported speech is usually changed according to the rules of the sequence of tenses.
 
• The verb "**is**" changes to "**was**" and "**has**" changes to "**had**" in reported speech.
 
• The pronoun "**he**" remains the same in the reported speech.
 
• The reported speech is introduced by a reporting verb and a conjunction "**that**".
 
• Therefore, the correct indirect speech of the given sentence is "*The lawyer told the father of the accused that there was a rumour that he had some connection in that crime.*"

Hence, **option 3** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: Incorrect as it uses present perfect tense "has been" instead of simple past tense "was".
 
• **Option 2**: Incorrect as it uses present continuous tense "is having" instead of past continuous tense "was having".
 
• **Option 4**: Incorrect as it uses present perfect tense "has had" instead of past perfect tense "had had".
